title: Research: adaptive QQ16 reads still need 66 ports; 45 optimal sets
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Add `research/qq16-adaptive-coordinate-reads/`: a scoped proof and finite certificate for adaptive, side-effect-free coordinate access on the rational QQ16 hidden-input family of [PR2354](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2354).

PR2354 establishes the fixed-set threshold of 66 ports and explicitly excludes adaptive choices. This contribution proves that every exact deterministic reader needs at least 66 distinct source-port reads on every input, regardless of adaptive choices, nonlinear computation or stopping rules. For input-independent random seeds, almost-sure exactness and termination on each rational input give the same lower bound almost surely by a countable-intersection argument.

The finite source geometry further classifies **all 45 optimal terminal read sets**. Every optimal set contains 22 mandatory ports and 44 of 45 coordinates participating in one relation. Port 77 can replace 44 specific ports in the predecessor's attaining set. Explicit rational decoders attain all 45 sets on the credited family. A proposed uniqueness strengthening fails and is deliberately rejected by a control.

These are information-access counts, not per-owner widths, native-line costs, recursive rank charges or a new kappa. The reader receives only complete original ordinary-port arrays and the zero inherited observations on this family. No source preprocessing, dense observation, changed call, input-dependent header or internal physical intervention is granted. Full QQ16 recovery, native access/retention/restoration, hosting, precision and all-size supplier admission remain unchecked. The selected frontier and frozen inputs are unchanged.

## Validation

On CPython 3.12.3, standard library only:

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/qq16-adaptive-coordinate-reads --check-only
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/qq16-adaptive-coordinate-reads
python3 -I -O -B research/qq16-adaptive-coordinate-reads/verify.py
```

The registered normal/optimized runs and four artifact tests pass. Direct output:

```text
PASS_QQ16_ADAPTIVE_READS defect=66 optimum=66 optimal_sets=45 nuisance_coordinates=29 controls=11 no_new_kappa
```

Evidence includes:

- A 66-by-66 integer minor directly on the 88-dimensional coefficient kernel, determinant `174085318024506601157689344`; a matching all-owner upper bound proves exact rank 66. This independently rechecks a credited premise.
- 896 registered nonzero-chart route identities, 17 actual owner evaluations, 29 explicit varying kernel coordinates and the one exceptional port 77.
- All 67 candidate read-set ranks, checked both on a kernel basis and by the complementary-column rank identity; 45 have rank 66, 22 have rank 65. All 44 exchanged decoders and 11,968 owner/basis equalities pass.
- Eleven rejecting mathematical/receipt controls; exhaustive adaptive choices on a 16-input binary oracle (147 cells), plus dense-vector and nonlinear-target controls.
- Relocated read-only replay; a corrupted optimal-set receipt, changed source bytes and a dropped source pin all reject under optimized Python.

`git diff --check` passes. Applying `patch.mbox` to a temporary index at origin/main reconstructs the exact committed tree `7ff75e844a5e98504b3b58b35f9ba3bee6c2fbdf`. Receipt formatting is immaterial; every canonical proof-relevant JSON field and scalar type is compared.

The registered replay was run again on the final package bytes before submission, under an 8 GiB memory cap: it passed in about 15 seconds and left the worktree unchanged. The counts are consistent: 96 - 29 = 67 candidate ports, of which 45 read sets have rank 66 and 22 have rank 65.

Not run: full native QQ16 trajectory/children, selected cold supplier replay, proof-assistant kernel, hosted CI, all-size/precision/outer multiplier checks, bounded-error randomized analysis, or the complementary second-axis witness. Written quantified proofs and finite checks are explicitly distinguished.

## Open next questions

All 45 optimal sets omit the same 29 ports C minus {77}. A hidden-input witness supported on those ports screens all 45 sets at once. This account's [PR #2384](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2384) gives one: a second-axis witness on ports 44, 49, 58 and 70 with zero permitted observations through the full schedule. All four ports lie among the 29 that every optimal set omits, so that witness is invisible to each of the 45 sets. That combination was checked here only by port membership; the witness's own proof and checks are in PR #2384. Only after full recovery survives should native access and retention be priced.

A separate question is a bounded-error distributional lower bound. It requires an explicit input distribution and success criterion; the zero-error countable-intersection argument does not establish it. See the README and structured TASK.json questions.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

Priority revision 4 helped steer the work to a concrete central interface. The shared board exposed several already-claimed alternatives. The main mathematical detour was useful: a source check falsified uniqueness of the optimal set and exposed 44 valid exchanges through port 77. A compact machine-readable list of a package's explicitly excluded hypotheses would make follow-ups easier to find without re-reading long thread histories.
